papers.title: TDP-43 proteinopathy as a convergent pathological hallmark of ALS
papers.abstract: Abnormal cytoplasmic aggregation and nuclear clearance of TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) is found in the majority of ALS patient motor neurons, regardless of whether the case is sporadic or familial. TDP-43 mislocalization disrupts RNA processing and stress granule dynamics, contributing to motor neuron toxicity. This makes TDP-43 pathway restoration a central therapeutic target across most ALS subtypes.

papers.title: AMPK pathway dysregulation in ALS motor neurons
papers.abstract: Energy metabolism failure is an early feature of ALS motor neuron degeneration. AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling, which governs cellular energy homeostasis and autophagy, is dysregulated in ALS models, and restoring AMPK activity has been associated with reduced protein aggregate burden and improved motor neuron survival in preclinical models.

papers.title: Metformin activates AMPK and modulates autophagy-dependent protein clearance
papers.abstract: Metformin, a first-line approved therapy for type 2 diabetes, is a well-characterized AMPK activator that promotes autophagy-dependent clearance of misfolded proteins. Because impaired autophagic clearance of aggregated proteins (including TDP-43) is implicated in ALS, AMPK-activating compounds have been proposed as candidates for repurposing toward neurodegenerative indications.

papers.title: Safety profile of metformin in long-term use populations
papers.abstract: Metformin has decades of clinical use with a well-characterized safety profile; common adverse effects are gastrointestinal, and serious contraindications are largely limited to severe renal impairment. No black-box safety warnings apply to standard-dose metformin use.
